name: CADMIZORB-PLUS
sourceDescription: Calcium Carbonate 500mg + Calcitriol 0.25 mcg + Vitamin k₂7 45 mg + Methylcobalamin 750mcg + Magnesium 20mg + Boron1.5mg+ Zinc 7.5mg Soft Gel Capsules
displayDescription: Calcium carbonate, calcitriol, vitamin K2-7, methylcobalamin, magnesium, boron and zinc soft-gel capsules

clinical.summary: Ramnova soft-gel capsule combining calcium carbonate 500 mg and calcitriol 0.25 mcg with vitamin K2-7, methylcobalamin 750 mcg, magnesium 20 mg, boron 1.5 mg and zinc 7.5 mg. Calcitriol is the active form of vitamin D, so this product should be used under the supervision of a healthcare professional.
introduction: CADMIZORB-PLUS soft-gel capsules combine calcium carbonate with calcitriol 0.25 mcg, the active form of vitamin D, plus vitamin K2-7, methylcobalamin (vitamin B12), magnesium, boron and zinc. It is used to treat calcium deficiency and to support bone health, including in people with osteoporosis.

Take it at the same time each day, exactly as your doctor prescribes, and do not take more than advised. Because calcitriol is a strong form of vitamin D, your doctor may check your blood calcium during treatment. Tell your doctor about any other medicines and supplements you take, especially other vitamin D or calcium products.
uses: Supporting bone health in osteoporosis and low bone density

benefits.text: Calcium is needed for strong bones and teeth, and for normal nerve, muscle and heart function. Calcium carbonate tops up the calcium in your diet, and calcitriol, the active form of vitamin D, helps your gut absorb it. Magnesium and zinc also support normal bone metabolism.

In osteoporosis, bones become thinner and more likely to break. Calcium with active vitamin D helps maintain bone mineral density, while vitamin K2-7 activates proteins that help bind calcium into bone. Your doctor may prescribe it alongside other osteoporosis treatment.

sideEffects: High blood calcium with long-term or excessive use (see warnings)
clinical.howToUse: Take this medicine in the dose and for the length of time your doctor advises. Swallow the capsule whole with water; do not chew or break it. Taking it with or after a meal can help calcium absorption and reduce stomach upset.
clinical.howItWorks: Calcium carbonate supplies calcium, the main mineral in bones and teeth. Calcitriol, the active form of vitamin D, increases the amount of calcium the gut absorbs. Vitamin K2-7 activates proteins that help bind calcium into bone, while magnesium, zinc and boron support normal bone metabolism. Methylcobalamin is an active form of vitamin B12, needed for healthy nerves and red blood cells.
warnings: Calcitriol can raise blood calcium too high (hypercalcaemia). Your doctor may check your calcium and kidney function regularly, especially when starting treatment or changing the dose.
Avoid other vitamin D products, including high-dose vitamin D supplements, unless your doctor advises them.
The risk of high calcium is greater if you are immobile for long periods, for example after surgery.
If you are on long-term kidney dialysis, your doctor will decide whether this product is suitable, because it contains magnesium as well as calcitriol.
Tell your doctor if you have kidney disease, kidney stones or a heart rhythm problem.
contraindications: High blood calcium (hypercalcaemia) or a condition that causes it
Calcium deposits in body tissues (metastatic calcification)
Allergy to any ingredient of the capsule
interactions: Thiazide water tablets, such as hydrochlorothiazide, can increase the risk of high calcium.
High calcium can increase the risk of heart rhythm problems in people taking digoxin.
Vitamin K2-7 can reduce the effect of blood thinners such as warfarin or acenocoumarol, so your doctor may need to check your INR.

Calcium, magnesium and zinc reduce the absorption of some antibiotics (tetracyclines and ciprofloxacin), thyroid medicine, iron and bisphosphonates. Take them at least 2 hours apart, or as your doctor advises.
Cholestyramine and sevelamer reduce calcitriol absorption, and corticosteroids can reduce its effect.

safetyAdvice.note: It is not known whether alcohol interacts with this medicine. Heavy drinking also weakens bones, so limit alcohol and ask your doctor.
Use only if your doctor advises it. Calcitriol needs careful supervision during pregnancy.
Calcitriol passes into breast milk. Your doctor may monitor calcium levels in you and your baby.
Not expected to affect your ability to drive.
Tell your doctor if you have kidney disease, are on dialysis or have had kidney stones. The dose may need adjusting and your calcium checking.
Tell your doctor if you have severe liver disease, as the dose may need adjusting.

quickTips: Take it at the same time each day, preferably after a meal.
Do not take other vitamin D or calcium supplements unless your doctor advises it.
Keep at least 2 hours between this capsule and iron tablets, thyroid medicine, or antibiotics such as ciprofloxacin or doxycycline.
Include calcium-rich foods such as milk, curd, paneer, ragi and green leafy vegetables.
Drink plenty of water, and tell your doctor if you have had kidney stones.
See your doctor if you notice excessive thirst, frequent urination, nausea, constipation, confusion or unusual tiredness, which can be signs of high calcium.

name: ESORUSK-D
displayDescription: Esomeprazole 40 mg and domperidone 30 mg sustained-release capsules

clinical.summary: Ramnova capsule combining esomeprazole 40 mg, a proton pump inhibitor that reduces stomach acid, with domperidone 30 mg in sustained-release form, a prokinetic agent.
introduction: ESORUSK-D capsules combine esomeprazole 40 mg, which reduces stomach acid, with domperidone 30 mg in sustained-release form, which helps the stomach empty faster. It is used to treat gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (GERD), relieving heartburn, acid regurgitation, bloating and nausea.

Take one capsule on an empty stomach, 30 to 60 minutes before a meal, exactly as your doctor prescribes. Common side effects include headache, diarrhoea and dry mouth. Domperidone can affect heart rhythm, so tell your doctor about any heart problems and every other medicine you take.
uses: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (GERD), including heartburn and acid regurgitation

benefits.text: In GERD, stomach acid flows back into the food pipe, causing heartburn and irritation. Esomeprazole lowers acid production, which relieves symptoms and allows the food pipe to heal. Domperidone helps food move through the stomach faster, reducing bloating, fullness and the backflow of acid. Your doctor will decide how long you need to take it; do not stop or continue it without their advice.

sideEffects: Abdominal pain, diarrhoea, constipation or wind
clinical.howToUse: Take this medicine in the dose and for the length of time your doctor advises. Swallow the capsule whole on an empty stomach, 30 to 60 minutes before a meal. Do not chew, crush or open it.
clinical.howItWorks: ESORUSK-D combines two medicines. Esomeprazole is a proton pump inhibitor that blocks the pumps in the stomach lining that produce acid. Domperidone is a prokinetic that increases the movement of the stomach and intestines, helping food pass through faster and reducing reflux, bloating and nausea. The sustained-release form releases domperidone gradually through the day.
warnings: Domperidone can affect heart rhythm (QT prolongation). The risk is higher in people over 60, at higher doses and with other medicines that affect heart rhythm. It should be used at the lowest effective dose for the shortest possible time, as decided by your doctor.
Long-term use of esomeprazole, especially beyond 3 months, may lower magnesium and vitamin B12 levels and increase the risk of bone fractures.
It may slightly increase the risk of certain gut infections.
Tell your doctor before starting if you have unexplained weight loss, difficulty swallowing, vomiting of blood or black stools.
contraindications: Heart conditions such as heart failure, or a known abnormal heart rhythm (QT prolongation)
Bleeding, blockage or perforation of the stomach or intestines
Use with strong CYP3A4-blocking medicines such as ketoconazole, itraconazole or clarithromycin, or with the HIV medicine nelfinavir
Allergy to esomeprazole, similar acid-reducing medicines, domperidone or any other ingredient
interactions: Medicines that affect heart rhythm, such as some antiarrhythmics, antipsychotics like haloperidol, and antidepressants like citalopram or escitalopram, should not be combined with domperidone.
Esomeprazole can reduce the effect of clopidogrel, so the two should not be used together.
Esomeprazole can change the levels of warfarin, methotrexate, digoxin, phenytoin and diazepam, so your doctor may need to monitor you.
Esomeprazole reduces the absorption of some antifungals, such as ketoconazole and itraconazole, and the HIV medicine atazanavir.

safetyAdvice.note: It is not known whether alcohol is safe with this medicine. Alcohol can also worsen acid reflux, so limit it and ask your doctor.
Use only if your doctor considers that the benefits outweigh the possible risks.
Not recommended. Domperidone passes into breast milk and may affect the baby.
May cause drowsiness, dizziness or blurred vision. Do not drive until you know how it affects you.
Your doctor may need to adjust the dose or review treatment if you have severe kidney disease.
Not recommended in moderate or severe liver disease. Tell your doctor if you have any liver problem.

quickTips: Take it 30 to 60 minutes before your first meal of the day.
Avoid large, late or spicy meals, and limit tea, coffee, chocolate and alcohol, which can worsen reflux.
Avoid lying down for 2 to 3 hours after eating, and raise the head of your bed if symptoms are worse at night.
Get urgent medical help if you notice a fast or irregular heartbeat, fainting or fits.
See your doctor if you have severe or persistent watery diarrhoea, or if your symptoms do not improve.
Do not take it for longer than your doctor advises. Domperidone is used for the shortest time needed.

name: PIPROSHOT 4.5g
displayDescription: Piperacillin and tazobactam injection

clinical.summary: Ramnova injection combining piperacillin, a broad-spectrum penicillin antibiotic, with tazobactam, a beta-lactamase inhibitor. For use in hospital and clinical settings under medical supervision.
introduction: PIPROSHOT 4.5 g is an injectable antibiotic that combines piperacillin 4 g, a broad-spectrum penicillin, with tazobactam 500 mg, which protects piperacillin from bacterial enzymes. It is used in hospital to treat serious bacterial infections, including severe pneumonia, complicated urinary tract and abdominal infections, skin and soft tissue infections, and fever in patients with very low white blood cell counts.

It is given by a doctor or nurse as a slow infusion into a vein, usually every 6 to 8 hours. The most common side effect is diarrhoea. Tell your doctor straight away if you have ever had an allergic reaction to penicillin or any other antibiotic.
uses: Severe pneumonia, including hospital-acquired and ventilator-associated pneumonia
Complicated urinary tract infections, including kidney infection (pyelonephritis)
Complicated skin and soft tissue infections, including diabetic foot infections
Bloodstream infections linked to any of the above
Fever in patients with very low white blood cell counts (neutropenic fever) due to suspected bacterial infection

benefits.text: Piperacillin with tazobactam is active against many bacteria that cause hospital-acquired and ventilator-associated pneumonia, including Pseudomonas. Treating the infection promptly helps clear the lungs, ease breathing and reduce the risk of complications.

benefits.use: Complicated urinary tract and abdominal infections
benefits.text: Infections of the kidneys, urinary tract or abdomen are often caused by a mix of bacteria. Its broad range of activity covers many of these organisms, helping to control the infection and stop it spreading to the bloodstream.

benefits.use: Skin, soft tissue and diabetic foot infections
benefits.text: Deep skin and diabetic foot infections can involve several types of bacteria. This combination helps stop the infection spreading and supports healing alongside proper wound care.

People with very low white blood cell counts, for example during chemotherapy, can develop life-threatening infections. Starting a broad-spectrum antibiotic such as this one quickly is an important part of their care.

sideEffects: Pain, swelling or redness where the infusion is given
clinical.howToUse: This medicine is given only by a doctor or nurse in a hospital or clinic. It is dissolved and given as an infusion into a vein over about 30 minutes. Your doctor will decide the dose and how long treatment lasts, based on the infection and how well your kidneys work.
clinical.howItWorks: Piperacillin is a penicillin antibiotic that stops bacteria from building their cell walls, so they burst and die. Many bacteria make enzymes called beta-lactamases that destroy penicillins. Tazobactam blocks these enzymes, so piperacillin can work against a wider range of bacteria.
warnings: Serious, sometimes life-threatening allergic reactions, including severe skin reactions, can occur. Tell your doctor about any previous antibiotic allergy.
It can cause a serious bowel infection (Clostridioides difficile colitis). Report severe or persistent diarrhoea.
It may cause bleeding problems and low potassium levels, so your doctor may check your blood during treatment.
It contains a significant amount of sodium. Tell your doctor if you are on a low-salt diet or have heart failure.
In seriously ill patients it may slow kidney recovery, particularly with vancomycin. High doses can rarely cause fits, especially in people with kidney problems.
contraindications: Allergy to piperacillin, tazobactam or any other penicillin
A previous severe allergic reaction to any beta-lactam antibiotic, such as a cephalosporin or carbapenem
interactions: Probenecid increases the levels of piperacillin and tazobactam in the blood.
People taking blood thinners, including heparin and warfarin, may need more frequent blood clotting tests.
Piperacillin can raise methotrexate levels, which may need monitoring.
It can prolong the effect of muscle relaxants such as vecuronium used during surgery.
Using it with vancomycin increases the risk of kidney injury. Aminoglycoside antibiotics must be given separately, not mixed in the same infusion.

safetyAdvice.note: No harmful interaction is known. Avoiding alcohol can help your recovery from infection.
Used during pregnancy only when your doctor considers it clearly needed.
Small amounts pass into breast milk. Your doctor will weigh the benefits; watch your baby for diarrhoea or rash.
Its effect on driving has not been studied. Do not drive if you feel dizzy or unwell.
The dose is reduced in kidney disease, and your kidney function will be monitored, especially if you are seriously ill.
No dose change is usually needed, but tell your doctor about any liver problem.

quickTips: Before the first dose, tell your doctor or nurse about any past allergy to penicillins, cephalosporins or other antibiotics.
Tell staff immediately if you develop an itchy rash, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing during or after the infusion.
Complete the full course your doctor prescribes, even if you start to feel better.
Report diarrhoea that is severe, watery or bloody, or that continues, even weeks after treatment ends.
Report any unusual bleeding or bruising.
If you use hormonal contraception, ask your doctor whether you need extra protection.

name: URSORAM 300/150mg
displayDescription: Ursodeoxycholic acid tablets — 150 mg and 300 mg presentations

clinical.summary: Ramnova ursodeoxycholic acid tablets, available in 150 mg and 300 mg strengths. Ursodeoxycholic acid is a bile acid used in the management of certain liver and gallbladder conditions.
introduction: URSORAM tablets contain ursodeoxycholic acid, a bile acid, in 150 mg and 300 mg strengths. It is used to dissolve cholesterol gallstones and to treat certain long-term liver conditions, including primary biliary cholangitis. It works by improving the flow of bile and lowering the cholesterol in it, which helps gallstones dissolve and protects liver cells.

Take URSORAM after a meal with water or milk, exactly as your doctor prescribes. Treatment usually lasts several months or longer, so keep taking it even if you feel better. The most common side effect is diarrhoea or loose stools. Tell your doctor about any other medicines you take, and if you are pregnant or breastfeeding.
uses: Dissolving cholesterol gallstones in people whose gallbladder is still working
Liver disease associated with cystic fibrosis

benefits.text: Ursodeoxycholic acid lowers the amount of cholesterol in bile, which allows small cholesterol stones in a working gallbladder to dissolve slowly. This can take several months, so take it regularly for as long as your doctor advises. Your doctor may arrange scans to check progress.

In PBC, the small bile ducts inside the liver are gradually damaged and bile builds up. Ursodeoxycholic acid improves bile flow and protects liver cells from harmful bile acids, which can slow the disease and improve liver test results. It is usually taken long term.

benefits.use: Liver disease associated with cystic fibrosis
benefits.text: In cystic fibrosis, thick bile can block the small bile ducts and damage the liver. Ursodeoxycholic acid helps bile flow more easily and protects liver cells. In the UK it is approved for this use in children aged 6 to 18.

sideEffects: Diarrhoea or loose stools (the most common side effect)
clinical.howToUse: Take this medicine in the dose and for the length of time your doctor advises. Swallow the tablet whole with water or milk; do not chew or crush it. Take it with or after food.
clinical.howItWorks: URSORAM contains ursodeoxycholic acid, a bile acid that occurs naturally in small amounts in the body. It reduces the cholesterol the liver releases into bile, which helps cholesterol gallstones dissolve. It also replaces more harmful bile acids, improves bile flow and protects liver cells from damage.
warnings: Liver function should be checked regularly during treatment
Not recommended during pregnancy unless your doctor considers it clearly necessary. Women who could become pregnant should use non-hormonal contraception.
contraindications: Complete blockage of the bile ducts
Acute inflammation of the gallbladder or bile ducts
Allergy to ursodeoxycholic acid or any other ingredient of the tablet
interactions: Antacids containing aluminium or magnesium (such as magaldrate), cholestyramine and colestipol can reduce absorption. Take ursodeoxycholic acid at least 2 hours apart from them.
Medicines containing oestrogen, including hormonal contraceptives, can raise cholesterol in bile and may reduce its effect on gallstones.

safetyAdvice.note: It is not known whether alcohol is safe with this medicine. Limit alcohol and ask your doctor.
Not recommended unless clearly necessary. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor.
Only very small amounts are expected to pass into breast milk. Ask your doctor before use.
Not expected to affect your ability to drive.
Limited information in kidney disease. Tell your doctor if you have kidney problems.
Used to treat certain liver conditions. Take only as prescribed, with regular liver tests.

quickTips: Take it after meals with water or milk, at the same time each day.
Avoid high-fat, oily meals and limit alcohol.
If you get diarrhoea, drink plenty of fluids and tell your doctor if it continues.
Your doctor will check your liver tests regularly, especially in the first few months.
Get medical help quickly for worsening jaundice, severe itching, dark urine or ongoing abdominal pain.
Don't stop taking it without speaking to your doctor.
